title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan

epigraph.quote: You can't predict. You can prepare.
epigraph.author: Howard Marks, Oaktree memo, 2001

web_blocks.html: Let me argue the bull case the way its smartest owner would, using only numbers on file. FY2026 consolidated revenue grew 39.5% to ₹132.9 crore [27]. In the first half of FY2027 consolidated revenue grew 20.4% to ₹64.82 crore, and standalone revenue grew 26.1% to ₹64.92 crore, with standalone EBITDA of ₹21.07 crore, a 32.5% margin, and standalone profit after tax up 69.5% [21]. Orders in hand reached ₹302.35 crore at September 2026 against ₹232 crore at March, helped by a ₹92.95 crore digital-twin order from Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority, and the sales pipeline stands at ₹625.57 crore [21][12][15]. Recurring revenue rose 46.2% in the half and is now 43.5% of sales, up from 37.5% [21]. Management guides to FY2027 growth of 25-27% and wants days sales outstanding below 200, down from 260 [16].

Four mechanisms could turn that into compounding. First, the product is hard to rip out once a city runs its building permits on it, and SoftTech rule engines serve more than 1,500 cities in 18 states [15]. Second, the pay-per-use model charges every plan as it is scrutinised, so revenue rises with construction activity rather than with licence sales; it was ₹31.72 crore in FY2026, up 59% on the audited note's base and 38.6% on management's own base [1][16]. Third, the Civit products are being re-used for ports, airports and industrial corridors, with JNPA as the first reference [21]. Fourth, the TDR exchange taps a market the company puts at about ₹8,000 crore of annual transfers in Mumbai, where a 0.5% fee per trade would be ₹40 crore a year if the exchange captured all of it; first-half revenue from it was about ₹2 crore [14][16][21]. If those four land together, operating leverage does the rest, and the bull case value of ₹813 is what a 55-times multiple on ₹14.78 of earnings looks like.

Now the other chair. Reported profit is thin. FY2026 consolidated profit after tax was ₹5.33 crore and earnings per share ₹3.57, less than half of the ₹7.87 earned in FY2019 [27][37]. Free cash flow was negative in every year from FY2019 to FY2026; in the five years to FY2026 it consumed ₹26 crore after development spending, and ₹83 crore of new equity filled the gap [27][31][32][33][34][37]. The credit-loss charge of ₹12.49 crore in FY2026 was 1.4 times pre-tax profit, and roughly 40% of gross trade receivables are more than a year old [27]. Return on invested capital was about 4% [27]. In Q2 FY2027 consolidated profit after tax was ₹0.21 crore, down 35.7%, against ₹3.63 crore at the parent, because losses in overseas subsidiaries and a 77% tax rate cut the group number [21][30].

The moat is narrower than the pitch. Telangana replaced SoftTech's permit system with a rival's within about four years [22], a free government platform, UPYOG, offers a building-plan module to any state [23], and the “80% share” claim that appears in earlier decks is not repeated in the FY2026 annual report [15]. One order, JNPA, equals about 70% of FY2026 revenue and 31% of the September order book; without it, orders in hand are about ₹209 crore, below the ₹232 crore at March [21][15]. Two customers made up 19.7% of FY2026 revenue, a first for the last three years [15]. The auditor's report records quarterly returns to banks that differed from the books by as much as ₹15.95 crore [27]. And the stock has no institutional owner and trades about ₹20 lakh a day [37][42].

Here is my own judgement. The bull evidence is about growth and it is good: one-year guidance has been met, orders have risen and the new lines are real products. The bear evidence is about conversion, whether growth becomes cash and profit for shareholders, and it is stronger because it rests on eight consecutive years of audited statements rather than on guidance. The pipeline's closest business label is CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL. SoftTech's condition is not a cycle. It is proof that the money coming in from customers and shareholders ends up as cash a shareholder can keep. That proof does not yet exist, and a price of 119 times earnings does not allow time for it to arrive.

web_blocks.takeaway: Scenario values and probabilities are analyst estimates. Change them when audited cash flow, credit-loss charges, order conversion or customer mix change.

web_blocks.html: Why these probabilities? The bear case gets 30% because the record gives it plenty of precedent: eight years of negative free cash flow, a credit-loss charge larger than profit, an order book that excluding JNPA is shrinking, a customer-concentration first, a state that replaced the platform and overseas subsidiaries that are still loss-making [27][22]. The base case gets 50% because management has delivered its one-year targets, FY2026 growth of 40% and a standalone first half on pace (group revenue grew 20.4%, below the 25-27% guide), while missing the long ones: the February 2024 roadmap promised 3 times revenue in 3 years and delivered 2.03 times, and the 25-million-dollar topline target was pushed from 2024 to 2026 and then replaced by a rupee target [16][18]. The bull case gets 20% because it needs a port or airport win beyond JNPA, a first major overseas permit deployment, TDR volumes that are today about ₹2 crore a half and an end to group tax drag, all within about eighteen months, and none of the four has yet produced material revenue [21].

Here is what that probability set means for the price. With the bear case fixed at 30%, ₹425.90 is fair only if the bull case has a 31% chance rather than 20%. The expected outcome is ₹369 and the median outcome, the base case, is ₹299. From today's price that is a 13.5% expected loss and a 29.8% loss in the single most likely outcome, against a 90.9% gain in the one outcome in five that goes well.

Be honest about how wide the margin is. Move 10 points of probability from the bear case to the bull case on my own base and the weighted value is about ₹431, roughly 1% above the price. A 13% annual return from ₹425.90 to March 2028 needs about ₹504, which only a bull-weighted view reaches. Each point of FY2028 EBITDA margin is worth about ₹0.85 of EPS, or about ₹42 a share at 50 times, and each five points of tax rate about ₹23. So the verdict leans on one number, FY2028 earnings power of about ₹6 a share. If audited results point to ₹9 or more, the base value rises to ₹450 and the answer changes. That is why the reopen conditions are about earnings and cash, not about the share price.

Now the verdict rule. The pipeline's anti-hedging rule says a non-rejected call must offer at least 1.5 to 1 reward-to-risk from its support zone, or it is rejected. The reference support band is ₹373.07-₹384.43 with an invalidation level at ₹365.17 [41]. From the top of that band, risk is ₹19.26 a share. The base value of ₹299 sits below the band, so the reward in the most likely outcome is negative: a reward-to-risk of -4.4 to 1. Only the bull case clears the hurdle. A WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT label would imply that a better price turns this into a buy, and it would not until the price reaches about ₹218-₹242, where the base case pays 1.5 to 1 against a ₹205 stop (a 15% stop). That band is 43% to 49% below ₹425.90 and sits on the March 2026 low of ₹218.65. I would rather say plainly what that means: new money is rejected at this price, with a defined set of conditions that would reopen the file.

web_blocks.caption: Three-horizon decision and trigger card
rows: Short-term trading / momentum
AVOID; no edge

Timing gate is CAP_REJECTED, turnover is about ₹20 lakh a day and up-day and down-day volume are balanced. Needs a close above ₹451 on twice the usual volume and a weekly close above ₹462, and even then Chapter 9's valuation test still fails.
Medium-term inflection
CONDITIONAL; growth is real, cash is not

FY2027 audited free cash flow after capitalised development at or above zero (FY2026: about -₹1.3 crore), days sales outstanding under 200, a credit-loss charge under ₹5 crore, and group pre-tax margin above 10% (FY2026: 6.7%).
Long-term compounding
NOT PROVEN

Return on invested capital above a 13% cost of capital (about 4% in FY2026), reinvestment falling toward 12% of revenue, repeat large orders beyond JNPA, and a second state or country adopting the permit platform without price concessions.
web_blocks.takeaway: The business verdict is CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL with KPI health PASS_WITH_WATCH. The new-capital verdict is REJECTED at the current price.

web_blocks.html: Those three rows read in plain English as follows. For a trader there is nothing to do. For someone willing to wait a year the question is whether the FY2027 audited cash-flow statement, due around May to June 2027, shows that cash conversion has turned. For a long-term owner the question is whether SoftTech becomes a business that spends 12 cents on the dollar to maintain its products instead of 27, and earns more than it costs to fund it.

Next, your portfolio. The same-session positions ledger shows 18 equity holdings worth ₹37.17 lakh, cash of ₹5.75 lakh (13.4% of net worth) and a net worth of ₹42.92 lakh, with no SoftTech shares. The holding action is therefore NOT_HELD and the number of shares to sell is zero. If you wanted exposure despite this verdict, 2% of net worth would be about 201 shares and 5% about 504, which is 4.5% and 11.2% of an average day's volume. The risk budget for a rejected setup is zero, so the sizing table in Chapter 8 recommends nothing.

web_blocks.takeaway: Allocations total 100%. Snapshot figures are from TradingView and Screener via the same-session snapshot [41]; the candidates named were not underwritten in this run.

web_blocks.html: The redeployment logic is simple. No pool of money is freed by this verdict, because you do not own SoftTech, so I define the reviewed capital as your next marginal unit and send 100% of it to cash. The shortlist names listed carry better return-on-equity and growth numbers on the same snapshot, and AJMERA (market-facts ledger: Stage 3) and COFORGE (ledger: Stage 2) both carry a snapshot Stage 2 label with a BUY_AT_CMP_NO_FOMO posture, but a snapshot is not an underwriting and I will not allocate to a company I have not re-underwritten in this run. The outside peers I screened were chosen to test SoftTech's multiple, not as buy candidates.

web_blocks.takeaway: Every row has zero shares because you hold none. A price trigger alone never changes the verdict; the business evidence has to move as well.

web_blocks.html: Read the alert table as a list of questions, not instructions. The first row is the one that matters. If the FY2027 audited cash-flow statement shows that operating cash after development spend is at least zero, days sales outstanding under 200 and a credit-loss charge under ₹5 crore, then the base case in Chapter 7 needs to be rebuilt, because EPS and the multiple the market would pay for it both move. With FY2028 EPS of ₹9 instead of ₹6, for instance, a 50-times multiple is ₹450, which would put the stock at fair value rather than rich. I am not predicting that; I am telling you what the evidence would have to do.

A note on the limits of this work. The market-wide Stage 2 scanner failed twice because the browser dashboard could not clear its filters, and in any case it covers companies above ₹1,000 crore of market value, so SoftTech would not appear on it. The Q2 FY2027 earnings call was scheduled for 13 November, after the results; I could not retrieve its transcript, so Q2 commentary here comes from the filed results and the presentation [10]. The benchmark had no verified 13 November bar, so the report is dated to 12 November. The last TradingView print of ₹425.90 is provisional, and all percentages in Chapters 7 and 9 are measured against it; against the ₹420.95 verified close the weighted value is 12.5% below the price, and the verdict is unchanged. The company-reported figures contain several definitional conflicts, which Chapters 2 to 6 document, and where I could not resolve them I used the audited note.

What changes the verdict: audited FY2027 free cash flow after capitalised development at or above zero together with days sales outstanding under 200, or a price inside ₹218-₹242 with the Chapter 7 base case intact. Until one of those happens, new capital is REJECTED and the next marginal unit stays in cash.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: You and I can admire the business and still decline the price. The discipline is to write down in advance what would change our minds: audited cash flow, collection days, a second large order. If the evidence arrives, we change our view. If the price falls to where the base case pays, we look again. We do not move the goalposts because the stock moved.
